walkthroughs.body_html:
Applied Anatomy and Physiology — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Applied Anatomy and Physiology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Applied Anatomy and Physiology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many bones are in the adult human skeleton?

options: Elbow
Knee
Hip
Wrist

mcqs.q: What type of joint is the knee?
options: A hinge joint.
Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.
A ball and socket joint.
A pivot joint.

mcqs.q: How long does the ATP-PC system last at maximum intensity?
options: Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.
About 2 minutes.
Unlimited duration.
About 10 seconds.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between strength and power?
options: Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.
Strength is maximum force; power is force times speed of movement.
They are the same thing.
A pivot joint.
